title: Sequoia Systems - Embeddings & Reranking Discovery
summary: Initial discovery to understand Sequoia's embedding + rerank use case: integrating vector DB (Milvus/Weaviate/Pinecone), target QPS and latency, dimensionality and storage concerns, hybrid BM25 + embeddings scoring, and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing and dedicated pilot plan, security docs, and schedule a technical deep-dive benchmark with sample dataset.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
next_steps: Maya: Send tailored pricing and Dedicated pilot proposal by 2027-05-07
Aaron: Schedule technical deep-dive and benchmark session w/ Priya for week of 2027-05-10
Lena: Share sample dataset and current embedding pipeline notes by 2027-05-06
Tom: Provide expected SLOs and compliance checklist items
action_items: Maya Chen: Email pricing + Dedicated pilot doc (due 2027-05-07)
Aaron Patel: Setup benchmark runbook + invite (due 2027-05-10)
Lena Ortiz: Upload 10k sample docs and current embeddings export (due 2027-05-06)
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-05-04 15:00 PDT | Duration: 46 min | Attendees: Maya, Aaron (Redwood); Lena, Tom, Priya (Sequoia)

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
00:04 Speaker 2 (Lena): Yeah good here, thanks Maya.
00:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): Cool, quick agenda  we want to understand your current embedding pipeline, vector DB choices, latency / throughput targets, and then talk about Redwood's Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options for reranking. Aaron will take the technical deep-dive.
00:24 Speaker 3 (Tom): Sounds good, high level  we're building a semantic search + rerank layer for our docs and product Q&A. Right now we use Elastic for BM25 and an in-house embedding service, but costs and latency at scale are growing.
00:38 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Got it. Can you walk me through current QPS and typical query complexity?
00:45 Speaker 3 (Tom): Peak reads are around 350 QPS across regions, typical 95th percentile latency target is < 200ms for search and rerank combined. Our current re-ranker is a small cross-encoder hosted on CPU which is expensive.
01:02 Speaker 4 (Priya): And we also have hybrid queries where we do BM25 to prefilter then embed rerank top 100. So we care about both vector DB throughput for ANN and the cost of running a reranker per candidate.
01:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): That hybrid flow is common  many teams prefilter with lexical then embed+rerank. With Redwood we can host embeddings, or you can keep your vector DB and call our Hosted or Dedicated re-rankers. Curious what vector DB you're evaluating  Pinecone? Milvus?
01:34 Speaker 3 (Tom): We prototyped with Pinecone and Milvus; Pinecone seemed simple but costs scale. We're also experimenting with Weaviate for open source flexibility.
01:44 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Ok. Two integration patterns we see: 1) Use Redwood for embeddings + push vectors to your DB (we support standard dims and formats), 2) Use your embeddings and have Redwood host the reranker and call into your vector DB via API/connector. Which approach are you leaning to?
02:03 Speaker 4 (Priya): Prefer to keep vectors in our VPC/DB for compliance, so likely option 2; but we also want Redwood to run the reranker close to where the vectors live  asking about Dedicated or Private.
02:17 Speaker 1 (Maya): Makes sense. Quick note on deployment modes: Hosted is fastest to try (Redwood-managed cloud), Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation, Private gives you a customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem) for strict compliance.
02:34 Speaker 3 (Tom): What does Dedicated look like in terms of throughput per GPU for a typical cross-encoder reranker?
02:40 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Depends on model size and quantization, but as a ballpark a modern quantized cross-encoder on 2xA100-sized pool can do ~100-200 reranks per second per GPU when reranking top-100 with batched inference. With batching and caching you can push much higher. Our Optimize tooling recommends batch sizes and KV-cache settings based on your prefix reuse.
03:04 Speaker 4 (Priya): When you say KV cache, do you mean key-value attn cache for the model or some prefix cache? We use the term differently internally.
03:12 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Good callout  I mean the model KV cache for auto-regressive, but for rerankers we rely more on batching and ephemeral cache of candidate embeddings; Redwood also supports prefix/embedding caching at the request router to reduce repeated ANN calls.
03:29 Speaker 1 (Maya): A couple of practical Qs  what embedding dimensionality are you using? 768? 1024? 1536?
03:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): Our prod embeddings are 1024 dims right now from an in-house model. Storage is about a concern  we store ~60M vectors.
03:46 Speaker 3 (Tom): Yes storage and retrieval costs bite. If we moved to 768 dims we could save a third, but we worry about performance drop.
03:55 Speaker 2 (Aaron): That's tradeoff territory  Redwood's Optimize can run regression tests with heldout queries to recommend lowest dim that doesn't hurt MRR. Also for hybrid flows, we sometimes combine smaller dims for ANN and feed higher-dim embeddings to re-ranker only, or use asymmetric hashing.
04:17 Speaker 1 (Maya): Do you have regulatory constraints or encryption/KMS needs?
04:21 Speaker 3 (Tom): We're in finserv vertical for a subset of customers, so SOC2 is must, and for some accounts we need customer-managed keys and VPC-only access.
04:31 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and customer-managed HSMs; we can run Private in your cloud with our control plane or fully on-prem if required. For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private networking as well.
04:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): How about SSO and RBAC? We need SCIM + SAML for provisioning and fine-grained role controls.
04:53 Speaker 1 (Maya): We support SAML, SCIM provisioning, and per-route RBAC. Audit logs are included in our enterprise bundle with retention options. We'll send the security pack.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Tom): Let's talk costs  ballpark for reranking workloads where we do 350 QPS at peak, reranking top-100, what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated?
05:12 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Hosted is usage-based and flexible  good for early-stage, but cost-per-rerank can be higher because it's multi-tenant. Dedicated becomes cost-effective once you hit sustained throughput, especially with reserved GPU capacity. We can run a cost model for your actual query distribution.
05:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): We should model token costs, GPU hours for reranker, and ANN storage/reads. Also we can show mixed routing: critical customers routed to Dedicated with SLA, others to Hosted.
05:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): For our pilot we want to test three things: integration with Milvus in our VPC, throughput at 350 QPS with <200ms p95, and MRR improvement over current pipeline.
05:54 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Perfect. For Milvus we usually recommend using their vector index with HNSW for recall and Faiss/IVF for throughput depending on vector size. We'll need sample data to tune index params.
06:07 Speaker 3 (Tom): Any gotchas with dimensionality and ANN index size? Our 60M x 1024 vectors are heavy.
06:14 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Index memory is large  Milvus/HNSW memory can be multiple x vector store if you keep full index in RAM. Consider productizing on IVF + quantization (OPQ or PQ) for production. We can bench different approaches during pilot.
06:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): How do we handle freshness and vector updates? We have frequent document churn.
06:33 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yep we ingest nightly batches and some streaming updates. Rebuilds are expensive.
06:38 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Incremental updates are supported by most vector DBs; for heavy churn you can shard by time window or use hybrid store with warm/cold tiers  Redwood can route queries to warm indices for recent docs and cold store for archival.
06:54 Speaker 1 (Maya): Any concerns about network latency if reranker in Redwood Hosted calls into your VPC vector DB?
07:01 Speaker 3 (Tom): That's a worry  we don't want cross-cloud hops.
07:05 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Right. For that pattern Dedicated or Private is recommended to colocate reranker near DB. We also support connectors that run within your VPC to minimize egress.
07:15 Speaker 4 (Priya): Can you run a small proof-of-concept with limited data in our account?
07:19 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, we do pilots. Typical flow: get sample dataset, choose index params, run benchmark for latency/QPS and MRR, and iterate. For Dedicated pilot we can provision a small reserved GPU pool for a few weeks.
07:33 Speaker 3 (Tom): What's the timeline to get a bench set up?
07:36 Speaker 2 (Aaron): If we get samples this week we can have an initial bench next week. We'll need Priya to coordinate infra access and a contact to set up VPC peering or a connector.
07:48 Speaker 1 (Maya): I'll follow up with credentials and the pilot doc.
07:51 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Quick question on hybrid scoring  do you want to run re-rank scoring that combines lexical BM25 score with embedding similarity, or prefer two-stage with reranker override?
07:59 Speaker 4 (Priya): We currently linear-combine BM25 + cosine for scoring then rerank top 100 with a cross-encoder. Hoping to reduce candidate size while keeping recall.
08:11 Speaker 2 (Aaron): We can replicate that. Redwood supports custom scoring hooks and per-route model ensembles. We can also add learned weights and tune during pilot.
08:22 Speaker 3 (Tom): Any examples of customers that moved from Pinecone to Dedicated for cost reasons?
08:27 Speaker 1 (Maya): A few  we can share anonymized case studies in the follow-up.
08:32 Speaker 4 (Priya): What about dimensionality experiments  do you do automatic knockout tests?
08:36 Speaker 2 (Aaron): We run heldout eval sets and can compute MRR/Recall deltas for candidate dims. Often you can go from 1024 to 768 with <1-2% MRR loss depending on model. We'll show numbers from similar workloads.
08:51 Speaker 3 (Tom): Ok, security detail  we need SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest, KMS integration and audit logs with 12 month retention. Also need to know data residency in EU.
09:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): Redwood has SOC 2 attestation; our enterprise pack supports KMS and audit log retention options. For EU residency, our Hosted regions include eu-west and we can discuss Private deployments in your AWS account for strict residency.
09:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): Good. On-SLOs, to meet <200ms p95 for full flow (ANN + rerank) what are realistic expectations?
09:27 Speaker 2 (Aaron): If reranker is colocated and ANN is tuned for latency (small candidate set ~50-100) we often see combined p95 under 200ms; if network hops exist it can double. So colocated Dedicated/Private is safest for tight SLOs.
09:41 Speaker 1 (Maya): Let's recap next steps  Maya to send pilot + pricing + security docs, Aaron to set up tech deep-dive and benchmarking, Lena to share sample dataset and metrics, Tom to confirm SLOs and procurement timeline. Any other questions?
09:56 Speaker 2 (Aaron): One last  how do you measure quality for rerank? You mentioned MRR  do you have labeled pairs?
10:02 Speaker 3 (Tom): We have a small labeled set (~2k queries) and plan to expand. For now MRR and NDCG suffice.
10:09 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll also want to test adversarial queries and monitor quality drift.
10:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great, we'll include quality monitoring hooks in the pilot and set up alerts in Redwood Console.
10:20 Speaker 2 (Aaron): Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
10:24 Speaker 3 (Tom): Appreciate it.
10:26 Speaker 1 (Maya): Thanks all  talk soon.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions  e.g., "K V cache" vs KV-cache, "Micro-saws" (misheard) etc. References to connectors: "Milvus connector" and "VPC connector". Links mentioned: security pack (link), pilot runbook (link), pricing spreadsheet (link).
